findings.title: Entering Off leaves the arbiter's mode and tank set-point at the optimizer's last write
findings.claim: After the optimizer is set to Off, the pump-mode select stays on the last step's duty (Tuya: 'DHW (Hot Water)') and a Modbus pump's tank set-point stays on the space-step gate (40 against the configured 50), through three later cycles, where the brief's off row owes each written entity its baseline once (both circuits allowed, the configured tank set-point).
findings.mechanism: pump_arbiter._arbitrate's MODE_OFF branch only _forget()s the record; the baseline row (desired(coord, inp, None, now)) is written by pump_arbiter.release on unload alone, and off_restore.async_mode_change restores only registered consumers (the space set-point, the heat curve, MQTT). The module docstring states 'The mode, the hot-water set-point and the silent switch are not restored' and tests/features.py pins 'switching the optimizer off writes the space set-point's baseline back, once, and nothing else', so the fix changes a pinned rule against the D16 owner ruling of 2026-11-15.

findings.title: Supply switch, frequency, valve and circulation pump have no restore owner on off, unload or remove
findings.claim: Four written entities -- the heat-pump power switch (left off after an idle step), the compressor frequency number (45 against 70), the mixing-valve target (18 against 22) and the hot-water circulation pump (left off) -- stay at the optimizer's last value after Off, after unload and after the entry is removed, because none of their writers registers with off_restore.
findings.mechanism: off_restore restores only consumers registered at import (heat_curve, heat_curve_mqtt, pump_arbiter_space). pump_arbiter.switch_supply, coordinator._command_frequency, coordinator._command_valve_target and coordinator._async_set_pump only stop writing in MODE_OFF ('off writes nothing') and on unload; nothing writes their baseline back. After async_remove_entry no later setup can either, so a pump switched off on an idle step stays off.

findings.title: Unload during a held disinfection run leaves the tank set-point at the disinfection target
findings.claim: When the entry unloads (or is removed) while the integration holds the pump's disinfection program on, the tank set-point stays at the cycle target 60 instead of the configured 50, because release() computes its baseline row while the disinfection hold is still live.
findings.mechanism: coordinator.async_shutdown calls LegionellaGuard.async_release_switch (DisinfectionSwitch.release_blind turns the switch off but leaves memo True) and then pump_arbiter.release, whose desired(coord, inp, None) reads inp.disinfecting (the memo) in _dhw_target and so writes, or finds already written, the cycle temperature. The same row reads the action's dhw_reason legionella, so a plan-booked cycle step unloaded has the same seam.

findings.title: A space set-point restore that fails on entering Off is never retried while Off
findings.claim: If an off_restore write fails at the change into Off (a device briefly unreachable), it is not sent again over six hours of arbiter ticks and cycles after the device answers: the space set-point keeps the optimizer's gate (25, not the captured 45) and the heat-curve offset keeps +3 K (not the neutral 0), until a person toggles the optimizer or the entry unloads.
findings.mechanism: off_restore.async_restore runs only from async_mode_change (the transition into MODE_OFF) and async_unload_entry; a failure is latched (off_restore_<key>) and left armed 'so the next off or unload tries again'. pump_arbiter._arbitrate returns at MODE_OFF without consulting the armed record, so no state reachable without a person leads to the write.

enumerate.py d16-writes misses no writer: no hass.states.async_set, mqtt.async_publish or other .async_call receiver writes an actuator

leads.what: Under pump_duty_mode observe (and off) these writers are not gated by the duty mode: in m6_restore.py's duty_change arm the reloaded observe-mode coordinator writes the power switch, the frequency, the valve, the circulation pump, the heat-curve entity and both MQTT topics again (writes after trigger 1-2 each), against the observe/off row 'no write'. Whether those writers belong to the duty mode at all is M2's to grade.

After WORKER_FALLBACK_CAP=3 consecutive ProcessWorkerUnavailable the in-process solve is never tried again until the process route carries a job; a deterministic fault (a job that cannot be pickled, a child that cannot load it) leaves the plan stale and every actuator write stopped with no automatic release; a restart buys three solves. Not measured here: the guard is D1.M5's.

The hold universe is log_held calls only; write-gating latches without log_held are not lines: coordinator._freq_fallback (person-only re-arm, by its docstring), pump_arbiter ArbiterState.retry/misses, supply_hold.hold_supply, early_cutoff's hold, DisinfectionSwitch.memo. M5 ranged over the enumerator's 30; those latches were not tabled.

The baseline row's tank target reads the live action's dhw_reason legionella and the disinfection memo (D16-s3-03); any other caller of desired(None) (a stale plan, the lease end) carries the cycle target the same way: worth a timing/value check on the baseline row during a cycle step.
